URL: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-04/labour-leads-reform-in-uk-poll-in-latest-sign-of-burnham-boost
(Search snippet content — Bloomberg / Ipsos / YouGov, late July–early August 2026; own reporting language)

UK polling, early August 2026 (Andy Burnham PM since 20 July 2026):
- JL Partners: Labour 27%, Reform UK 25% — Labour leading Reform for the first time in more than a year ("Burnham boost").
- YouGov: Reform UK 23%, Labour 22% — Reform first nationally.
- Techne UK: Reform and Labour tied at 25% each.
- Aggregate: the so-called "Burnham bounce" has largely stalled roughly two weeks after Burnham entered Downing Street, with Reform surging back into first place in some polls.
- Ipsos: Reform UK holds a slim voting-intention lead over Labour, but Andy Burnham is preferred as PM over Nigel Farage and Kemi Badenoch.
- Immigration is a top voter priority at 48%, tied with the economy for first place.

Context (background): Keir Starmer announced on 22 June 2026 he would resign amid loss of confidence among MPs; Andy Burnham was acclaimed Labour leader on 17 July 2026 and became PM on 20 July 2026.
